title: Names Kept for Returning
text: The oldest register in {city_name} leaves space after every name. It began with travelers going to {dungeon_name}; the empty space was meant for whatever they would call themselves on return. The town kept the custom when the ink faded.
landmark_text: Names cut beside the road have a second, smaller line underneath. Most are empty. Beside one, someone carved: I came back. I still like my name.
book_text: The town copy records a keeper refusing to close the register. A name could be corrected by its owner. Nobody else was allowed to decide that a journey was finished.
witness_text: We keep a space for the returning name. If you visit {dungeon_name}, come back and tell us what you'd put there. Leave it empty if you like. I'll be glad to see you either way.
author: The local archive of {city_name}

event_notes.text: At supper, the keeper learned a traveler's name. By the time the cups were gathered, half the table was using it.
The delivery arrived. The receiver signed the ledger, then asked the carter whether anyone was waiting for them at home.
